First retrospective (runs 1-10). Headline: the loop generates good adjustments but has no channel to apply them - only 4 of 11 critique-proposed adjustments across 23 days ever reached LOOP.md or the scripts, and the branch-tips cache took 5 flaggings over 3 weeks to land. The graduation gate is technically met (0 false_positives, 0 escalations across 10 runs) but must NOT be read as evidence: false_positives is fed exclusively by a human [FP] mark that has never once been made, so 0 is an absence of measurement, not precision - the same silent-zero class as a mis-scoped test glob. Two thresholds have never fired and structurally cannot (cache hit rate <50% against an observed 0.96-0.99 band; 2x-trailing-median output tokens against a 17k-1.98M range). critique: Applied branch-staleness-by-commits-ahead, previously HELD the same day and then approved by explicit decision. Deviated from the literal proposal on purpose and said so in the ledger row: run 5 asked to replace tip-date staleness WITH commits-ahead, but commits-ahead measures divergence, not time - a branch 3 ahead and untouched 60 days would have scored identically to one created this morning. The real defect was narrower: git rebase preserves the author date and writes a new committer date, and the protocol never specified which one it read. So staleness now pins to the tip AUTHOR date, and ahead_by is recorded as a SEPARATE signal (0-ahead + stale = dead weight to delete; 12-ahead + stale = unmerged work at risk). Adding ahead_by threatened to reintroduce the per-branch API call whose removal took five proposals over three weeks, so the branch_tips cache was extended rather than bypassed: author_date refetches only on a branch SHA change, ahead_by also on a DEFAULT-branch SHA change since it is relative to a moving base, and pre-today cache entries with a bare date field are treated as a miss because there is no way to know which date they held. Ledger now 10 of 11 landed, 1 held, 0 outstanding.

adjustment.text: Staleness on tip author date; ahead_by as a separate divergence signal

critique: Applied cache-quiet-repo-pr-issue-results, previously HELD the same day then approved by explicit decision - and again deviated from the proposal text on purpose. Run 9 asked to cache a no-PRs/no-issues answer for repos confirmed quiet twice running. That is not the same shape as the branch_tips cache it was modelled on: branch_tips skips expensive calls only AFTER one cheap authoritative call proves nothing changed, whereas caching a quiet-repo negative has no detector at all and creates a window where a newly opened PR goes unreported - a false negative on a loop whose only job is surfacing things. Verified against gh 2.95.0 that gh search prs --owner supports --json, then smoke-tested it live: one call returned both open fleet PRs (TokenMonitor #1 and #2), matching STATE.md exactly. So the per-repo sweep across ~17 repos was ELIMINATED in favour of two fleet-wide calls rather than cached - same cost saving, zero staleness. Added an explicit --limit and truncation check, since gh search defaults to 30 and a truncated list reads as fewer open PRs. Ledger now 11 of 11 landed, 0 held, 0 outstanding - every adjustment proposed across runs 1-10 is applied.

adjustment.text: Fleet-wide gh search for PRs/issues instead of a per-repo sweep

The revised CACHE threshold fired for the first time (91.3% vs a 0.978 five-run median, 6.5pp below the 5pp trigger) and it is a low-volume artifact: today's entire sample is 39 input / 6,831 output tokens, essentially this triage run alone, so a handful of requests move the ratio. critique: Run 13. Cleanest fleet state the loop has seen: ZERO open PRs and ZERO open issues (down from 3 PRs), and all four stale remote branches are now 0 ahead, so every staleness finding this run is losslessly deletable dead weight. The empty gh search prs result was NOT taken at face value - it was re-verified with a per-repo gh pr list drill-down, because 'no open PRs' and 'the search source is broken' render identically in a digest and this loop's only job is surfacing things. The revised CACHE threshold cleared on its own (95.7% vs a 0.978 median, 2.1pp, inside the 5pp trigger) with no edit, and today was ANOTHER low-volume day (15,603 output tokens) - so the outstanding gate-cache-flag-on-min-volume adjustment now has one low-volume day that fired and one that did not, which weakens rather than strengthens run 12's case for it. Refinement 5 fired for the first time ever: claude-token-tracker held 1 dirty line (?? .claude/) unchanged across 3 runs. false_positives is NON-ZERO for the first time (1, loop-derived: the NMMTools 0-ahead pair, same recommendation ignored for 3 runs), which finally feeds the counter the L2 graduation gate reads. But feeding it exposed a mechanical defect, and that is this run's adjustment: noise-match-on-finding-identity-not-text. Refinement 1's literal test is 'byte-identical across 3 consecutive runs', yet every GitHub staleness item embeds an age in days that increments every run (20d -> 23d here), so no such item can EVER be byte-identical and the counter can never fire on its own terms - I counted the pair on the rule's INTENT, not its letter. That is the same un-fireable-check class the 2026-08-06 retrospective just removed from the spend and cache thresholds, reintroduced one refinement later. Fix: key loop-derived noise on a stable finding identity (repo + branch + recommendation), not on rendered text. Noisiest source was GitHub branch staleness again (4 of 16 findings), for the third run running. One process note: the batched local-hygiene sweep MISREPORTED Aether-OS-livetest as 1 dirty line when git status --porcelain actually returns 3; a direct re-run of the count is what caught it, and refinement 5's stale-WIP rule reads that exact number - a wrong count there silently flips a flag. Verify counts the flag depends on directly, never from inside a batched loop whose output was not spot-checked.

critique: Run 17. Fleet went from the quietest state on record to a small uptick: 1 open PR (new, TokenMonitorV2#1) where there were 0, issue count unchanged at 1 (Aether-OS#22, open on purpose). The PR resolves a Watch List item that had persisted since run 15 ("no PR backing reskin-phases-3-4") - local work had already moved on to a new reskin-phase-5 branch (19 and 20 ahead of main respectively, both pushed, so not at loss risk despite the size). Verified branch-tips cache diff caught exactly 3 changed/new branches out of 26 (agent-improvement/master via the sibling agent-learn loop's own commit, plus TokenMonitorV2's two reskin branches) and reused the other 23 - the cache is earning its keep. Two things this run adds to the record. First, false_positives is 1 (loop-derived), and it should not have taken this long to catch: the Aether-OS "1 commit on no remote branch" recommendation has been byte-identical since at least run 14 with zero human action, crossing the refinement-1 bar a run or more ago without anyone (loop or human) marking it - moved to Recent Noise now with an explicit decision ask (push, delete, or add to Human Decisions). Second, and this run's adjustment: refinement 5's stale-WIP check compares only the dirty-line COUNT run over run, and today it fooled itself - Aether-OS-livetest read as "unchanged for the 4th run" at 4 dirty lines, but the actual file set changed (e2e/livetest2.spec.ts is new, replacing nothing; the count coincidentally held). A repo can shed one file and gain a different one on the same day and still look stale under a count-only comparison. Fix: dirty-count-blind-to-content-churn - compare the file path set, not just the count, before crediting an unchanged run.
